podcast.body: A twin rocker from 'The Rise and Fall of Ziggy Stardust and The Spiders from Mars' album, "Suffragette City" became a staple on US rock radio airplay, along with the album's title track. This helped the album become Bowie's first to break into the Top 100 on the Billboard album chart in early 1973. "On US Radio, the album's title track and its twin rocker Suffragette City became rock-airplay stapes."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.body: Originally released as the B-side to David Bowie's 1972 single "Starman" from the "Ziggy Stardust" album, "Suffragette City" later achieved greater recognition and is arguably considered a more significant hit within Bowie's discography. "Suffergett City, originally the B side to starman from Ziggy Stardust, but hit arguably became the bigger hits in the Bowie canon."
